newsitem.title: SPAIN: Analysts divided on when Spain stocks may correct.
newsitem.headline: Analysts divided on when Spain stocks may correct.

text.p: The Madrid stock market's heady rise since January this year has left analysts divided over when an increasingly inevitable correction may take place.
Although they disagreed regarding short-term prospects on Tuesday, on a medium to long term horizon the outlook is still bright, they say.
"Current prices make you think of selling, although we may yet gain another one or two percent" said a dealer at Argentaria Bolsa.
"We've risen a lot in a little time, and short term the potential is running out. But the correction will not be substantial because medium to long term the trend will stay bullish," he added.
At 1000 GMT Madrid's general stock index was trading up 0.95 percent to 549.47. So far this year the index has risen 23 percent, while since April 2 alone, the rise is of 18 percent.
The Ibex-35 index of blue chip stocks is also near all-time highs. At 1420 GMT it was trading up 0.54 percent to 6,316.41.

"Short-term, or within two months, the general index could correct to around 500 points, and, from then on, its going to be volatile for the rest of the year," said Jose Manuel Castellano, head of strategy at BBV Interactivos.
"We think the correction will be inspired by New York," he added.
Another analyst said stocks' rise could continue.
"The market has heated up again, although both in terms of fundamentals and charts, it could carry on" he said.
For others, although gains so far this year were excessive, that was not a reason for the market to fall yet.

"These levels are awesome, and if the market was to rise 10 or 15 percent more, with the current economic backdrop, the message would clearly be to sell," said Alvaro Martinez, head of equities at AB Asesores brokerage.
Phillip Sardet, head of sales at Credit Lyonnais Securities also saw more upside.
"Taking into account the strength of the funds coming into the market as well as economic data, the conclusion is that the market is very strong and has upside," he said.
"If there is a consolidation, it won't be very big," he said.
Most analysts have already seen their year-end targets for the bourse beaten in four months.
"The rise has smashed our forecasts, but we'll wait another couple of weeks before fixing new targets," said one analyst.
